config.title: Styled Component Pattern

intro.title: Styled Component Pattern
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, reusable button component using the Styled Component Pattern in Angular. You'll learn how to encapsulate styles directly within a TypeScript component to keep your UI elements modular and self-contained. The core concept involves using Angular's component decorator to define inline styles, avoiding external CSS files for small, focused components. You'll work with the @Component decorator, template literals for HTML, and TypeScript to create a styled button that can be easily reused across your application.
intro.usecase: The Styled Component Pattern is widely used in enterprise Angular applications where consistent, reusable UI components are essential. You'll see this pattern implemented in design systems for dashboard widgets, data tables with custom styling, and branded form controls that maintain visual consistency across an application. Developers use this approach when building complex interfaces like admin panels, e-commerce product cards, or notification systems where each component needs its own encapsulated styling logic. This pattern helps teams scale UI development while ensuring maintainability and theme consistency across large applications.

objectives: Construct a reusable Angular component with encapsulated styles using the Styled Component Pattern
Apply CSS custom properties to create configurable style interfaces for components
Configure component inputs to control visual appearance through style bindings
Implement style encapsulation techniques to prevent CSS leakage between components
Manipulate component templates to integrate dynamic styling based on input properties
Initialize style configurations through component properties for consistent theming
Render styled components with conditional appearance based on application state

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core
steps.instruction: Import the Component decorator and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the same module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Angular core features
import { Component, NgModule } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component decorator and CommonModule are imported, enabling component creation and common directives.
successCriteria: Component and CommonModule are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Define the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator. Set the selector to 'app-root' and provide an empty template string.
steps.hint: Use the Component decorator imported in the previous step. The class should be named AppComponent and export it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator containing the selector and an empty template.
successCriteria: AppComponent class is exported with @Component decorator, selector is 'app-root', and template is an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the AppComponent class is exported and the @Component decorator has both selector and template properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Check that you're using the @Component decorator with the correct selector and template.

steps.title: Define a styled button component class
steps.instruction: Create a new component class named StyledButtonComponent with a @Component decorator. Place it below the AppComponent class.
steps.hint: Use the same pattern as AppComponent: export class StyledButtonComponent {} with @Component decorator above it.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of another component class
export class AnotherComponent {}
steps.expectedOutcome: A new StyledButtonComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, ready for styling and template.
successCriteria: StyledButtonComponent class is created with @Component decorator and exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the component, but make sure it's a class named StyledButtonComponent with @Component decorator and exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StyledButtonComponent class with @Component decorator is not properly defined. Review the pattern used for AppComponent.

steps.title: Add template and styles to the styled button component
steps.instruction: Add a template with a button element and inline styles to the StyledButtonComponent class.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator on the StyledButtonComponent class to define its template and styles.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledButtonComponent will have a template with a button element and inline styles defined.
successCriteria: StyledButtonComponent has a @Component decorator with a template containing a button element and inline styles.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the template includes a button element with inline styles.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StyledButtonComponent should have a @Component decorator with a template containing a button element and inline styles.

steps.title: Add input property to the styled button component
steps.instruction: Add an @Input() property named 'buttonText' to the StyledButtonComponent class to make the button text configurable.
steps.hint: Use the @Input() decorator from @angular/core to declare an input property. You'll need to import Input first.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledButtonComponent will have a configurable input property that can receive text from a parent component.
successCriteria: StyledButtonComponent has an @Input() property named 'buttonText' with type annotation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the @Input() decorator and named the property 'buttonText'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input property is missing or incorrect. Check that you've used @Input() and named it 'buttonText'.

steps.title: Add output event to the styled button component
steps.instruction: Add an @Output() event emitter named 'buttonClick' to the StyledButtonComponent class to emit click events.
steps.hint: Use the @Output() decorator from @angular/core and create an EventEmitter instance. This will allow parent components to listen for click events from your styled button.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledButtonComponent will have an output property that can emit events when the button is clicked, enabling parent components to respond to interactions.
successCriteria: The StyledButtonComponent class contains an @Output() decorator with an EventEmitter instance named 'buttonClick'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the @Output() decorator and created an EventEmitter instance named 'buttonClick'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The output event emitter wasn't properly added. Remember to use @Output() decorator and EventEmitter from @angular/core to create an event emitter property.

steps.title: Declare the styled button component in AppComponent
steps.instruction: Add StyledButtonComponent to the declarations array in the @Component decorator of AppComponent.
steps.hint: In the @Component decorator of AppComponent, find the declarations array and add StyledButtonComponent to it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent's @Component decorator will include a declarations array containing StyledButtonComponent.
successCriteria: StyledButtonComponent is added to the declarations array in the AppComponent's @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the declarations array might be missing or incomplete. Ensure StyledButtonComponent is included in the array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styled button component is not properly declared in AppComponent. Check the @Component decorator's declarations array.

steps.title: Add styled button to AppComponent template
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent's template, add the <app-styled-button> element to use your styled component.
steps.hint: Place the component selector inside the template string of the @Component decorator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template now contains the styled button component, making it ready to be displayed.
successCriteria: The AppComponent's template includes the <app-styled-button> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the <app-styled-button> element inside the template string of the AppComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styled button component is not yet present in the AppComponent template. Add the <app-styled-button> element.

steps.title: Bind input property to styled button
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, bind the buttonText property to the app-styled-button component using property binding syntax.
steps.hint: Use square brackets around the property name in the template to bind a value to it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template should have property binding that passes data to the styled button component.
successCriteria: The app-styled-button element in the AppComponent template uses property binding syntax with square brackets.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct property binding syntax with square brackets.
steps.feedbackWrong: The property binding isn't quite right. Remember to use square brackets around the property name to bind a value to it.

steps.title: Bind output event from styled button
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, bind the (click) event from the app-styled-button element to a handler method named handleButtonClick.
steps.hint: Add (click)="handleButtonClick()" to the app-styled-button element in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Binding an event in Angular template
<button (click)="onButtonClick()">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The styled button component will have its click event bound to a handler method in the parent component.
successCriteria: The app-styled-button element in AppComponent template has (click)="handleButtonClick()" binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the (click) binding to the app-styled-button element with the correct handler name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The click event binding is missing or incorrect. Add (click)="handleButtonClick()" to the app-styled-button element.

steps.title: Create handler method in AppComponent
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent class, add a method named handleButtonClick that logs a message to the console.
steps.hint: Add a public method inside the AppComponent class that uses console.log to output a message when called.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class now contains a handleButtonClick method that logs a message when invoked.
successCriteria: The AppComponent has a method named handleButtonClick that logs a message to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it's named exactly 'handleButtonClick' and includes console.log to output a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler method is missing or incorrect. Add a method named handleButtonClick to the AppComponent class that logs a message.

steps.title: Add multiple styled button instances
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add two more instances of the styled button component with different buttonText values.
steps.hint: Add two more <app-styled-button> elements after the existing one, each with a unique [buttonText] binding.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding multiple component instances
<app-styled-button [buttonText]="'First Button'"></app-styled-button>
<app-styled-button [buttonText]="'Second Button'"></app-styled-button>
<app-styled-button [buttonText]="'Third Button'"></app-styled-button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template will contain three styled button instances with different text labels.
successCriteria: Three <app-styled-button> elements exist in the template with unique [buttonText] bindings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some additional button instances, but make sure you have exactly three total with unique buttonText values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain three styled button instances with different buttonText bindings. Check that you've added two more <app-styled-button> elements.
